newsitem.title: INDIA: India IDBI sees mild rise in credit.
newsitem.headline: India IDBI sees mild rise in credit.

text.p: The chairman of the Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) on Monday said he saw some improvement in disbursement of credit to industries.
"There has been some improvement in the flow of applications since October/November," IDBI chairman S.H. Khan told reporters.
"People have started taking investment decisions," he said, referring to companies reviving industrial projects.

Khan said disbursement of credit growth upto the end of January was between 5.0 to 7.0 percent. He did not give comparative figures for the earlier period. He expected between 10 to 15 percent growth for the year ended March 31, 1997.
Analysts said loan payment was affected by a slowdown in several industries in recent months.
Khan was addressing a news conference to announce the company's plans to implement recommendations of consultant firm Booz Allen & Hamilton to restructure the organisation.
Booz Allen & Hamilton has recommended decentralisation, greater customer focus and establishment of profit centres.
IDBI is India's leading term-lending bank.
